description: Updates container images, Helm charts, vendor.txt, GitHub Actions and runners, Ansible collections and ansible-core, k3s, Flux, Terraform and its providers, app Dockerfiles, the Proxmox VM template image and the router's OpenWrt release. Non-major updates merge into main once .github/workflows/validate.yaml passes, outside 02:00-06:00 London so deploys miss the kured reboot window; majors wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.

customManagers.description: vendor.txt: the version column, located by the `# renovate:` comment above each entry
The Renovate CLI that scripts/check-renovate.sh runs in CI
The Flux release: the FluxInstance's distribution.version and the flux CLI that CI installs
kubeconform, installed by the validate-cluster action
pip packages pinned in app Dockerfiles
The Debian cloud image build behind the Proxmox VM template
The gateway's OpenWrt release, which router/build.sh builds and CI flashes

packageRules.description: The kubernetes manager also reports each manifest's apiVersion. Leave API migrations to humans.
Majors are manual: approve them on the Dependency Dashboard, then review and merge the PR. For pihole and cloudflared, the year rollover counts as a major.
ISC's stable Kea releases have even minor versions; odd minors are development releases. The two daemons release together (scripts/check-versions.sh).
GeoPulse's UI and backend release together (scripts/check-versions.sh).
RKE2's Multus chart pads its last component (v4.3.014), which strict semver rejects.

k3s and ansible-core upgrade one minor at a time (ansible/k3s/vars/versions.yml, .github/actions/ansible-setup/requirements.txt), as does alpine/k8s, whose tag is its kubectl version (deploy/setup/kured/proxmox-reboot/cronjob.yaml). Each minor gets its own branch. k3s and alpine/k8s minors automerge: scripts/check-versions.sh fails every branch but the next minor, and ansible/k3s/k3s.yml refuses to deploy a minor the nodes would skip.
...and each ansible-core minor waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.
A merged OpenWrt release is flashed onto the gateway (router/README.md). Patches merge on their own; a new release series (24.10 -> 25.12 is a major) waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.
The flux CLI in CI and the cluster's Flux move together (scripts/check-versions.sh).
The Go toolchain image and go.mod's go directive move together.

One branch for every non-major GitHub Actions bump, except the Python that setup-python installs (a Python minor can wait for months on ansible-core support, and would hold the others back) and the Flux action, which stays in the flux group.
A Python minor can outrun what runs on it (ansible-core lists the Pythons it supports). Each waits for approval.
Debian publishes cloud image builds every few days. The pin matters only when the template is rebuilt, so take at most one a month. The year rollover counts as a major.
Nothing applies these on merge: bootstrap/terraform is applied by hand. Leave the PR open as the reminder; merge it once the change is live.
ansible-galaxy passes a git role's whole URL to the github-tags datasource, which expects owner/repo, so the lookup fails.
